A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same computational model and experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original human experiments with 120 retained participants and computational simulations across ten games, including advice effects, ablations and generational learning.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds extended-training Double DQN results and qualitative diagnostic observations.

M1.justification: The VGDL world models, Bayesian inference, 20-particle implementation, language-guided proposals, planning and advice generation remain unchanged. The supplied prompts and inference algorithm also match; the new particle-count discussion does not change the adopted method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten games and individual, social and generational learning tasks. Extended baseline training retains this coverage. The added description of participants as adult English speakers documents the existing sample.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain the oracle, Double DQN and LLaMA-3.1-70B agent. Expanded references to ReAct and chain-of-thought describe the retained baseline, whose prompt is unchanged; Appendix K extends Double DQN's budget without introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix K adds Double DQN evaluation extending to 2,000 episodes, and Appendix D reports testing 10 rather than 20 particles. These are supplementary settings; the main participant allocation, 15-life protocol, nAUC metric and two-life, ten-generation design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine baseline sensitivity to extended training, the speed and reliability tradeoff between 10 and 20 particles, and LLM reasoning-trace failures in rule inference, planning and execution. The existing language-proposal ablation and message analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The stated 20 simulation runs per condition, interquartile ranges, standard errors and fixed-effect significance tests remain unchanged. The added analyses introduce no specified new seed counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures. New Figure 3 aggregates ten games rather than changing the run count.

E6.justification: Figure 10 adds extended-budget Double DQN outcomes, including successful learning in aliens, beesAndBirds, jaws and missileCommand. Appendix D adds qualitative particle-count findings. Main results, including human-advice nAUC gains of 0.12 for humans and 0.04 for models, remain unchanged; the new baseline outcomes use different budgets.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds a short combinatorial search-space argument reporting approximately 10^30 configurations for five objects, supplementing the retained main-text statement that the space exceeds 10^20. The probabilistic assumptions, inference equations and planning mathematics are unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly makes explaining human social learning the primary contribution and reduces the introduction's broader claims about scalable agents. The three central mechanisms and knowledge-transfer claims remain. Section 2 also changes the game-suite provenance from developed to reused.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific explanations for generational regressions, discusses approximate speaker likelihoods and particle-computation tradeoffs, and considers dependence on LLM language priors. Appendix K interprets extended-training failures and argues against longer LLM runs. These expand the existing interpretation and limitations without replacing the central account.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository address and reproducibility statement promising release, participant eligibility information, median completion time of 49.30 minutes and median pay of $10.41/hour. It specifies one A100 GPU and removes the earlier generational-study copy-paste restriction passage. The PDFs do not establish an actual recruitment or procedure change.

R1.justification: The discussion expands connections to program-based cognitive theories and executable world models, adding works such as Rule et al. (2020), Wei et al. (2022) and Lehrach et al. (2025). Appendix A more explicitly distinguishes inference of unknown dynamics from prior known-dynamics settings. Csibra and Gergely (2009) and Henrich (2016) are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction's detailed findings summary is condensed, the discussion is revised around cognitive modeling, and explanatory passages are expanded. v2 adds a reproducibility statement and appendix contents and retitles several sections. Most technical exposition, experimental reporting and prompt text remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference formatting, adds an aggregate Figure 3 and extended-training Figure 10, and moves v1's per-game Figure 3 to Appendix B as Figure 7. All eight original figures are retained, with accompanying relocation, renumbering and caption edits.

improvement.justification: The extended Double DQN evaluation provides useful context beyond v1's short-budget comparison, while added recruitment details, methodological explanations and clearer positioning improve transparency. The core empirical evidence remains unchanged. Gains are limited because particle sensitivity and LLM diagnostics remain qualitative, Figure 10 leaves aggregation details unclear, and the prediction about longer LLM runs is untested.
